routes.label: Count two preimages at every step
Turn the recurrence into repeated squaring

question: A sequence of complex numbers \(z_0,\) \(z_1,\) \(z_2,\) \(\ldots\) is defined by the rule \[ z_{n+1} = \dfrac{i z_n}{\overline{z_n}}, \] where \(\overline{z_n}\) is the complex conjugate of \(z_n\) and \(i^2 = -1.\) Suppose that \(|z_0| = 1\) and \(z_{2005} = 1.\) How many possible values are there for \(z_0?\)
solution:
The condition \(|z_0|=1\) keeps the entire sequence on the unit circle. Indeed, whenever \(|z_n|=1\), its conjugate is nonzero and
\[
|z_{n+1}|=\frac{|i|\,|z_n|}{|\overline{z_n}|}=1.
\]
Also, \(z_n\overline{z_n}=1\), so the recurrence is equivalent to
\[
z_{n+1}=iz_n^2.
\]
This form makes it useful to work backward from \(z_{2005}=1\).

For any target \(w\) of modulus \(1\), its predecessors satisfy \(z^2=-iw\). To see exactly how many there are, write \(-iw=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta\). The double-angle formulas show that
\[
u=\cos\frac{\theta}{2}+i\sin\frac{\theta}{2}
\]
is one square root, and \(-u\) is another. They are distinct and both have modulus \(1\). There are no others: any other root \(v\) satisfies \((v-u)(v+u)=0\), hence \(v=u\) or \(v=-u\).

Thus each target has exactly two valid predecessors. Distinct targets cannot share a predecessor, because the rule \(z\mapsto iz^2\) assigns each input only one successor. Consequently the number of possible values doubles at every backward step. Every valid initial value appears in this construction, and every constructed value produces a defined sequence ending at \(1\).

After \(2005\) backward steps there are \(\boxed{2^{2005}}\) possible values of \(z_0\), choice E.

solutionMethods.explanation:
Starting with modulus \(1\), every term has modulus \(1\), because the numerator and denominator in the recurrence have equal modulus. All denominators are therefore nonzero. Since \(z_n\overline{z_n}=1\), we have \(z_{n+1}=iz_n^2\).

To remove the factor \(i\), define \(w_n=iz_n\). Then
\[
w_{n+1}=i(iz_n^2)=-z_n^2=(iz_n)^2=w_n^2.
\]
Each step doubles the exponent of the starting value, so \(w_n=w_0^{2^n}\). Set \(N=2^{2005}\). The condition \(z_{2005}=1\) becomes
\[
w_0^N=i.
\]
Because \(|w_0|=1\), write \(w_0=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta\), with \(0\leq\theta<2\pi\). The power formula gives exactly the angles
\[
\theta=\frac{\pi/2+2\pi j}{N},
\qquad j=0,1,\ldots,N-1.
\]
These are \(N\) distinct angles in the required interval, and each produces a solution. They exhaust the possibilities because \(N\theta\) must differ from \(\pi/2\) by an integer multiple of \(2\pi\).

Finally, \(z_0=-iw_0\) converts these solutions into distinct valid initial values. Therefore there are \(\boxed{2^{2005}}\) possibilities, choice E.
solutionMethods.label: Turn the recurrence into repeated squaring
